description:
From the fz-kdt.186 refutation (2026-09-03, accb5cfbe). types/mod.rs:2432
runtime_type_predicate_tuple_arities removes a negated signature's ARITY
outright, where the list axis (runtime_type_predicate_list_shapes) removes a
shape only for an exact-empty / exact-non-empty negation. So the surface
`{any, any} & not({int, int})` -- non-empty, it holds {:ok, :ok} -- projects
to a RuntimeTypePredicate that admits nothing (`!p.overlaps(&p)`), and since
all three lowerings read one projection, an arm compiled for that surface
emits a test that always fails: a live arm that never fires (a value in the
surface falls through to later arms or the fail node). Reproducer:
    let carved = t.difference(t.tuple(&[any, any]), t.tuple(&[int, int]));
    assert!(!t.is_empty(&carved));
    let p = t.runtime_type_predicate(&carved);
    assert!(!p.overlaps(&p));       // admits NOTHING
Same family: a ListShapes axis whose only head is `none` (the fz-kdt.186
review's P2), and brand_of("Z") projecting to the all-none predicate
(requires_any widens only cofinite brand sets; no production caller today).
This was the root of the hole the 186 refuter closed in the seat (an
untested self-blind position could separate a pair); the seat is now robust
to it, the PROJECTION is not fixed. FIX: a same-arity negation must subtract
per POSITION into the shape (the way the list axis subtracts only exact
shapes), degrading to arity-only (over-approximate) when it cannot; never
to empty. Red-first: the reproducer as a unit pin, and a three-door fixture
with a clause over a carved tuple surface. Also correct the stale
finite_set.rs:112-114 sentence ("never to drop an arm or to justify a
seat" -- contained_in feeds test_inside, a drop conjunct since 143).
CONCORDANCE: fz-kdt.146 (the list-clause degrade rule -- the honest
precedent this axis should follow), fz-kdt.107/119 (the tuple axis's
origin), fz-kdt.186 (the seat made robust to it).

comments.text:
fz-kdt.194 raised the stakes on this projection defect, and measured the population it reaches so the argument stops being silently load-bearing.

fz-kdt.194 gives a SEPARATED adjacent pair a canonical order in specificity_order. Under fz-kdt.186 a fictional separation (two arms with DIFFERENT surfaces at a position where one projects to the empty predicate -- this ticket's shape) only meant "leave the pair alone"; under fz-kdt.194 it means "MAY REORDER". The seat's guard `early == late || early.overlaps(late)` still covers the case where both arms carry the SAME unrealizable surface; it does not cover two different surfaces where one projects to nothing.

That is still a routing no-op, one step further along: dispatch_row's preconditions are the very same observable_inputs Ty values, so an arm whose projected test admits nothing emits a row NO VALUE CAN TAKE, and moving an unreachable row past its neighbour changes no destination. fz-kdt.194's repair is adjacent-transpositions-only, so the dead row's own motion is the whole of the effect. The argument is written at the seam, in canonically_order_separated_neighbours' doc, naming this ticket.

MEASURED POPULATION (fz-kdt.194 build worktree, base ca23b676f + fz-kdt.194, release binary, all 604 fixtures2 fixtures). Every Separated verdict was classified as a FICTION when EVERY separating position is self-blind on one side (!p.overlaps(&p)):

  setting        separation readings   FICTION   arity-mismatch
  settled        172 (25 fixtures)     0         0
  arms:1         214                   0         0
  arms:3         214                   0         0
  arms:6         214                   0         0
  wrappers:1     186                   0         0
  wrappers:6     182                   0         0

So the fictional-separation population that reaches fz-kdt.194's rule is ZERO on this corpus, and no realizability conjunct was added there. If this ticket's fix lands, that stays zero by construction rather than by measurement. If instead the seat is ever tightened with a realizability conjunct, that is fz-kdt.186's surface and needs its own red-first gate.

fz-kdt.194 landed (04a10fb51) and MEASURED YOUR POPULATION: 0 fictional separations at settled and under arms:1/3/6 and wrappers:1/6, against 172/214/214/214/186/182 real separation readings on the same runs. So the defect you name is real in the calculator but has no corpus witness today. That mattered here because 194 makes "Separated" mean "may be canonically reordered" rather than "leave alone", so a fiction would license a reorder. 194 does NOT add a realizability conjunct; instead the unreachable-row argument is written at the repair's seam naming this ticket, and the measured zero is pinned. If you land a realizability conjunct, re-measure that census -- it should stay 0 and the arm-order gate should stay at 0 findings.

title: [BUG] runtime_type_predicate_tuple_arities drops an arity for ANY same-arity negation: `{any, any} & not({int, int})` (non-empty) projects to the empty predicate, so a live arm compiles to a test that never fires
